body:
<!-- plain-summary -->
When data is damaged badly enough that Wyrd cannot rebuild it, that loss is supposed to show up in the health metric operators watch — but a bug leaves those cases out, so the count of at-risk data can read as zero even while data is effectively lost. This matters because the one situation an operator most needs to notice, unrecoverable data loss, is exactly the one currently hidden from the dashboard.

**Summary.** In the reconstruction loop, a chunk whose loss is beyond the scheme's tolerance (`Assessment::Unrepairable`) has its obligation left queued but is **not** counted in the under-replicated durability metric — yet the code comment says it should be surfaced as under-replicated. Surfaced during the review of PR #394 (proposal 0014).

**Evidence** (`crates/custodian/src/reconstruction.rs`, main):
- The comment at the `Unrepairable` arm says the loss is beyond tolerance and to "Leave the obligation queued and **surface it as under-replicated**" (~line 142-144).
- But the arm body is `Assessment::Unrepairable => {}` (~line 145) — the chunk is dropped from `plans`.
- `emit_under_replicated(plans.len())` (~line 166) counts only `Repairable` plans, so an unrepairable chunk contributes to `reconstruction_queue_depth` (pre-assessment) but **not** to the `reconstruction_under_replicated` count.

**Impact.** The one class of loss an operator most needs to see — data past its redundancy floor, which reconstruction *cannot* fix — is the class the under-replicated gauge omits. A beyond-tolerance situation can read as `under_replicated == 0` (healthy) while chunks are effectively lost. This is also the honest-refusal signal M7 (proposal 0014) plans to drill; M7.2's DoD now depends on it, but the gap is a present-day defect independent of M7.

**Suggested fix.** Either count unrepairable obligations in the under-replicated emission (a separate gauge or folded into the same one with an `unrepairable` attribute), or, if the exclusion is deliberate, correct the comment and document where beyond-tolerance loss *is* surfaced. A distinct signal is preferable — "under-replicated but repairable" and "beyond tolerance, unrepairable" are different operator actions (wait for repair vs restore/accept-loss).

**Refs:** PR #394 review, `reconstruction.rs`, ADR-0011 (durability plane), proposal 0005 §custodian.

comments.body: Folded into **M7.2 (#481)** — the failover/DR milestone (plan of record: proposal 0014, §"Suggested PR sequence" step 2). The `emit_under_replicated` honest-refusal gap is closed as part of that leg: a beyond-tolerance chunk must be visible on the durability plane, not silently absent from the under-replicated count. Tracked under #486.

milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: Beyond-tolerance chunks are excluded from the under-replicated metric (comment says otherwise)
